_**We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Data & AI Architecture, based in Copenhagen or London, to lead our team of four Data, AI and Solution Architects and serve as the design authority for Pandora’s Data & AI platform. This is a genuine dual role. You’ll set the architectural direction and standards, while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge, review and approve the designs that matter.

_**Our target architecture is Databricks, including Delta Lake, medallion patterns and Unity Catalog, while Azure Synapse and its conformed enterprise models continue to power a significant part of the estate across supply chain, commerce, manufacturing, corporate technology and omni-channel.

A critical part of the role is leading the transition to Databricks: shaping the target architecture, determining where ownership sits as the platform evolves, and ensuring existing solutions remain coherent and supported throughout the journey.

The role is approximately 60% architecture and 40% people leadership. You’ll lead and develop four architects, but this is not a role where technical accountability is delegated to the team. Both sides of the role are real, and you’ll be expected to lead both.

**Scope and authority

**

• Design authority for Data & Analytics: approves data and AI solution designs, and can require rework, attach conditions to an approval, or withhold approval.

• Chairs the architecture review forum, setting its standards, cadence and quality gates, and deciding what requires review against what is already covered by an approved pattern.

• Resolves conflicting design positions across architects, lead engineers and delivery teams.

• Owns reference architectures, solution patterns, data contracts and architecture decision records — accountable for their adoption, not just their publication.

• Owns the team's roadmap, capacity allocation across workstreams, and budget, including engagement of external consulting resources.

• Translates and enforces the Data & AI architecture strategy set by the Global Director, and informs how it evolves.

**Job Responsibilities

****Architecture

**

• Set and enforce the standards for what is built on Databricks as the target architecture, what remains on Synapse for now, and what is retired — and on what evidence.

• Decide how data products are aligned: source-aligned versus domain-aligned versus consumer-aligned, where ownership and stewardship sit, and where a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) serves better than distributed ownership.

• Review technical designs from solution architects and lead engineers against platform standards; give feedback that changes the design, not just documents it.

• Define and evolve reference architectures, solution patterns and data contracts so that quality is built in rather than inspected in.

• Lead design sessions with architects, engineering and business stakeholders on complex or contested problems.

• Oversee transitional architectures through to legacy decommission, maintaining business continuity and closing the parallel run.

**AI architecture

**

• Set and enforce architecture standards for agentic systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation, guardrails and observability.

• Set and enforce architecture standards for ML systems: feature reuse, training and serving topology, model lifecycle, and monitoring for drift.

• Approve AI solution designs with enough depth to arbitrate them on the technical merits, and in line with AI policy and applicable regulation.

**Governance and regulation

**

• Embed privacy-by-design and personal data handling requirements into platform patterns, particularly across commerce and omni-channel.

• Maintain computational governance: data quality frameworks, contracts and lineage as platform capability rather than project effort.

**Team leadership

**

• Line management for four architects: coaching, performance, career development, hiring.

• Establish ways of working — review process, documentation standards, quality gates — and hold the team to them.

• Represent architecture in leadership forums, steering committees and cross-functional planning.

• Keep architects hands-on and embedded with engineering teams; architecture produced at a distance from delivery does not land.

**What You Will Have Done By Month 12

**

• A published and adopted standard for what is built on Databricks, with evidence of designs changed by it.

• A clear model for data product alignment and ownership, applied on live work rather than documented in isolation.

• An architecture review forum running to a predictable cadence, with a visible ADR record and a known path for challenging a decision.

• Approved agentic and ML reference patterns in use.

• At least one legacy component fully decommissioned, not just superseded.

• A development plan in place for each of the four architects, and any open roles filled.

**Essential Experience

**

• 5+ years designing and delivering production data platform solutions at enterprise scale, hands-on.

• At least 2 years line-managing technical specialists, including performance management, career development and hiring.

• Has held a design approval or architecture governance mandate, including declining designs and making that decision hold.

• Has led a platform migration or a parallel-run estate through to legacy decommission.

• Deep working knowledge of Databricks (Delta Lake, medallion, Unity Catalog) as a target architecture, plus enough Azure Synapse (star schemas, conformed models, dedicated pools) to govern what remains there, and pipeline orchestration with ADF or Databricks Workflows.

• Has designed source-aligned, domain-aligned and consumer-aligned data products, with a clear view of where distributed domain ownership beats a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) and where it does not.

• Has implemented or governed a domain ownership model — data mesh or similar — including the federated governance and stewardship that makes it work.

• Has architected agentic and ML systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation and guardrails; feature and model lifecycle, serving, and monitoring for drift.

• Has set architecture standards that others adopted — solution patterns, reference architectures and architecture decision records.

• Has implemented data quality frameworks, data contracts or computational governance in production.

• Holds an architectural position under delivery pressure, and judges well when to concede.

• Communicates architecture clearly to technical and business audiences, including solution designs, ADRs and data flow diagrams.

• Understanding of retail, manufacturing, finance or supply chain business processes and how data flows through a business.

**Desirable

**

• Familiarity with EU AI Act obligations and enterprise AI governance.

**Did we get your attention?

**We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

Senior Gameplay Programmer on WHAT THE CAR?

Do you love working in small, creative teams turning wild ideas into a reality? What about having creative and technical ownership from ideation through to release? Read on!

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

WHAT THE CAR? is our absurdly silly racing adventure game which addresses fundamental questions such as… What if a car had legs? Or a jetpack? Or secretly identified as a sailboat? First launched in 2023 on Apple Arcade and now also on Steam, it has gained a steady following of dedicated fans who have contributed hundreds of thousands of community-built levels.

We’re looking for a Senior Gameplay Programmer to help us continue to build upon CAR’s success by expanding upon its absurdly silly universe! We believe the best people to come up with ideas are the ones implementing them, so we expect a high degree of creativity and game design knowledge from our Gameplay Programmers, in addition to their crazy tech skills. This role involves around 60% programming and 40% game design.

**Here’s What That Looks Like Day To Day

**

• Build and ship gameplay code. You’ll implement features end-to-end in an existing Unity/C# codebase and ship regularly in a live environment.

• Generate design ideas. You’ll take part in shaping features, articulate intent, evaluate tradeoffs, and iterate through discussion with the team.

• Keep the game healthy. Fix bugs, improve systems, review test videos, and document findings so issues don’t come back to haunt us.

• Extend and refine what’s there. You’ll build on existing mechanics, making them more robust and enjoyable for players.

• Support and collaborate. You’re part of a small, closely knit, cross discipline team where people help each other reach their goals.

• Prototype and let go. Not everything ships, and that’s fine. Comfort with iteration and refactoring is part of the job.

**You’re a great match if

**

• You have 8+ years of commercial game development experience, having shipped at least two games as part of a team

• You have strong Unity and C# skills. You’re comfortable navigating a shared codebase and writing maintainable code you’d be proud to hand off

• You care about stability, performance, and long-term maintainability, and you leave systems better than you found them

• You genuinely value collaboration and working very closely with every member of the team

• You approach other people’s ideas with openness and try to understand the intention before giving feedback or pushing back

**Nice to have

**

• Experience working on live games

**Requirements For Any Job At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership - you spot problems, design and implement creative solutions that push projects forward

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture

• You value a positive work environment

• You contribute to making the studio a fun and supportive place

**Practicalities

**

• Primarily work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen

• Only open to candidates who are already eligible to work in Denmark as we don’t offer relocation support or visa sponsorship for this role

• 37-hour work week, with flexible work hours

• No crunch, we put people before deadlines

• Our working language is English

**We offer

**

• Silly but ambitious projects

• The chance to contribute to great games that reach millions of players

• A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights and team events

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

• Six weeks of paid vacation

• Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Pension plan and private health insurance

• Endless amounts of coffee

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, which is played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 50 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make everyone laugh. To do so, we focus on exploring comedy through gameplay. We like to break player expectations, use wonderful music, slick art, and create a quirky atmosphere. We experiment a lot, and it doesn’t always work out, but we always learn something.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games - and we believe diversity makes for better teams. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and will challenge us and our way of doing things.

Do you enjoy turning complex business questions into clear insights and practical recommendations?

Scan Global Logistics is looking for a Strategy Analyst to join our Group Transformation team.

This is an opportunity for someone early in their career who wants to work close to senior management and gain exposure to strategic priorities, business performance and transformation initiatives across a global organisation.

You do not need to have all the answers from day one. What matters is that you are analytical, curious, commercially minded and comfortable getting into the detail.

What you can expect

• You will join a global business with significant ambitions and an active transformation agenda.

• Broad exposure across the organisation and the opportunity to work closely with experienced leaders on real business challenges.

• For the right person, we expect the scope and responsibility to grow quickly. This is a strong opportunity to build a career within strategy, transformation or general business leadership.

• A straightforward, collaborative environment where you can challenge the status quo while staying focused on getting things done.

The role

As Strategy Analyst, you will support strategic and transformation initiatives across Scan Global Logistics.

You will work with data, business cases and management information, but the role is broader than pure financial analysis. You will help us understand business problems, identify opportunities, structure decisions and follow initiatives from idea through implementation.

Your work could range from analysing the performance of a business area or testing the assumptions behind an investment case to supporting a major transformation programme or preparing material for senior management.

In short, you will help turn data and complexity into decisions and action.

Your key responsibilities

• Analyse business performance, operational data and strategic opportunities

• Build financial models, business cases and scenario analyses

• Support strategic and transformation projects across functions and geographies

• Help structure complex or ambiguous business questions

• Track progress, value creation and key performance indicators

• Prepare clear decision material and presentations for senior management

• Work with colleagues across Finance, Operations, Commercial, our Regions and other functions

• Challenge assumptions and help ensure decisions are based on facts

• Support implementation and follow-up when initiatives move from analysis into execution

• Contribute to ad hoc strategic analyses and projects for senior management

Who are we looking for?

You probably have 1–4 years of relevant experience, although we are more interested in your capabilities and potential than the exact number of years. Your background could be from:

• Management consulting

• Corporate strategy or business development

• FP&A or commercial finance

• Business intelligence or analytics

• Transaction services

• A graduate programme or similar analytical role

You may also be a strong recent graduate with relevant internships and an excellent analytical foundation.

We imagine you have a degree within business, economics, finance, engineering or another analytical discipline.

What matters most

We are looking for someone who:

• Is genuinely strong with numbers and analytical problem-solving

• Can structure a problem before jumping to the answer

• Is comfortable working in Excel and PowerPoint

• Is curious about how a business actually works

• Can translate analysis into a clear recommendation

• Is pragmatic and willing to get into the detail

• Communicates clearly and simply

• Takes ownership and follows things through

• Is comfortable working with different stakeholders and cultures

• Wants to learn quickly and take on increasing responsibility

Experience from the logistics industry is not required but would be a plus. We focus on finding someone with the right analytical ability, curiosity and drive.

Why join Scan Global Logistics?

At SGL, you will join an international logistics company with an entrepreneurial culture, high ambitions and a strong belief that results are created by people who take responsibility. Our DNA is built on Respect, Integrity, Entrepreneurship & Fun.

At Scan Global Logistics, we value people who are straightforward, collaborative and willing to challenge the status quo while staying focused on getting things done.

Interested?

Send your CV and application through the SGL career portal. We review applications on an ongoing basis and will close the process when the right candidate has been found.

For further information, please contact Nikolaj Lei Jacobsen, Global CTO, on +45 4332 4641 or visit

www.scangl.com.

atNorth is a leading Nordic data center company providing cost-effective, scalable high-density colocation and built-to-suit services to industry-leading organizations across Iceland, Sweden, Finland, and Denmark.

With sustainability at our core, our data centers run on renewable energy and are designed according to circular economy principles. Through innovative design, power efficiency, and intelligent operations, we deliver reliable, secure, and high-performance infrastructure.

Headquartered in Reykjavik, Iceland, atNorth operates eight data centers across the Nordics, with additional sites under development in Finland, Denmark, Sweden and Norway.

We combine world-class technology with a people-first culture built on collaboration, ownership, and trust, empowering our teams to grow, take responsibility, and make a real impact.

By joining our international team, you will help shape the future of sustainable digital infrastructure.

**Strategy Manager at atNorth

**Are you passionate about building strategy?

We are looking for a Strategy Manager to help define and drive atNorth's future growth and strategic direction. This is a highly visible role working closely with the CEO, Executive Committee, Board, and senior business leaders to identify opportunities, solve complex business challenges, and ensure atNorth remains at the forefront of the rapidly evolving Nordic data center market.

Focusing heavily on strategy development, you will lead analyses, challenge assumptions, identify opportunities, and develop recommendations that influence critical decisions across growth, power, sustainability, commercial development, and corporate strategy. Reporting to the Director of Strategy and working as part of our Strategy team, you will collaborate closely with our existing Strategy Manager, combining strategic thinking with practical execution to turn ambitious goals into tangible outcomes.

This is a unique opportunity to influence the direction of one of the fastest-growing data center platforms in the Nordics. You will have direct exposure to executive leadership and play a key role in decisions that shape the future of sustainable digital infrastructure across the region. You'll join a collaborative, international team where curiosity, ownership, and impact are valued, and where your work will directly contribute to atNorth's continued success.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Lead the development and refinement of atNorth's corporate strategy, ensuring alignment with long-term business objectives.

• Keep a pulse on market trends, customer demand, competitor activity, technology developments, and broader industry dynamics to identify risks and opportunities.

• Translate market insights and business intelligence into strategic recommendations that support growth, competitiveness, and long-term value creation.

• Partner with executives, business leaders, and functional teams to evaluate strategic initiatives and priorities across the organisation.

• Support strategic planning, decision-making, and Board preparation activities alongside the Executive Committee and senior leadership team.

• Lead strategic projects and cross-functional initiatives from concept through implementation.

• Develop compelling business cases, market assessments, and strategic presentations for senior stakeholders.

• Support the development of power, sustainability, commercial, and geographic growth strategies that are critical to atNorth's long-term success.

• Engage with internal and external stakeholders to gather insights that inform strategic planning and decision-making.

• Act as a trusted advisor and thought partner to senior leadership on strategic opportunities and challenges.

**Your profile:

**

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Strategy, Industrial Management, or a related field.

• 5+ years of experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, business development, strategic planning, or related disciplines.

• Demonstrated experience developing business strategies and influencing strategic decisions at a senior level.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to turn complex information into actionable recommendations.

• Experience presenting to executive leadership teams, boards, or senior decision-makers.

• Excellent stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence without direct authority.

• Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to engage audiences ranging from operational teams to executives.

• Professional proficiency in English.

• Experience within the data center, energy, utilities, infrastructure, technology, or other capital-intensive industries is considered a strong advantage.

**About the atNorth Culture

**We believe that sustainable success starts with the wellbeing of our people. For us, an open, transparent, and inclusive culture is more than a priority, it is the core of how we lead and innovate.

We don’t just talk about culture; we nurture it. Through regular one-to-one engagements and monthly wellbeing surveys, we listen carefully to our teams, ensuring that every voice is heard and every opportunity for improvement is embraced.

We recognize that innovation and collaboration thrive where people feel truly connected, which is why we come together each week to share ideas, strengthen relationships, and nurture a sense of belonging, sometimes over a simple breakfast and good conversation.

At atNorth, we are building a community where you can do your best work and shape a sustainable future together.

Are you passionate about connecting digital strategy with hands-on execution to drive measurable marketing impact across European markets?

As our new Digital Marketing Manager, Western Europe, you'll shape and deliver the regional digital marketing agenda across 16 Western European markets, combining strategic direction with hands-on activation that strengthens customer engagement, lead generation, and conversion.

What you will be doing

As a key member of the Western Europe Marketing team, you'll create impact by translating business priorities into connected, measurable digital experiences that drive customer engagement and marketing effectiveness across one of Grundfos' most important regions.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Set and drive the digital marketing direction for Western Europe across 16 markets, translating regional business priorities into a clear digital roadmap aligned with global platforms, frameworks and best practices.

• Plan, execute and optimise multi-channel digital campaigns across websites, email, social media and search, aligned with regional priorities and customer journeys.

• Drive web performance and local optimisation across Western Europe, including SEO/GEO, traffic development and digital customer journeys, identifying opportunities to improve discovery, engagement and conversion.

• Track, analyse and report on digital performance, campaign ROI and KPIs, using A/B testing and performance insights to identify trends and deliver actionable optimisation recommendations.

• Support marketing technology adoption, automation, lead scoring, nurturing workflows and CRM integration to improve lead quality, conversion and alignment with Sales.

• Identify and translate emerging digital trends, including AI-driven discovery and changing search behaviour, into opportunities, while building digital capabilities and supporting execution across local teams.

What makes you a great fit

Above all, you're a strategic yet hands-on digital marketing professional who thrives at the intersection of planning and execution, with strong stakeholder management skills and a passion for turning data into better customer experiences. We'd also imagine that you have:

• 5+ years of experience in digital marketing roles covering strategy, campaign activation, and performance optimisation across multiple markets or regions.

• Hands-on expertise across the digital ecosystem, including web/CMS, SEO, paid media, marketing automation (e.g. Marketo), analytics, and lead management.

• Experience working in international matrix organisations, enabling collaboration across global, regional, and local teams.

• A strong analytical mindset with the ability to translate performance data into clear actions and priorities.

Why you'll love working here

Day to day, you can look forward to:

• A working environment built around your needs, with flexible hours, home working opportunities and parental support.

• Annual bonuses, health insurance and a strong focus on well-being activities.

• Three days' additional paid leave for volunteering.

• On-demand training and structured development programmes to support your growth.

Valuing our differences helps us see possibilities where others can't. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all abilities, experiences, and backgrounds. As part of our commitment to a safe and compliant hiring process, final candidates may be required to undergo a background check, subject to applicable local laws and regulations.

About Grundfos

Grundfos is one of the world’s leading water technology companies with more than 19.000 employees in 60+ countries all over the world. Our skills commit us to pioneering solutions to the world’s water and climate challenges and improve the quality of life for people. We dare to do things that others cannot or dare not do, as we believe innovation is not only a business opportunity, but an obligation. And what really matters to us is not short term profit, but the impact we make. By becoming part of our united powerful team, you too can drive this change no matter your role.

An inclusive team

We believe that the key to a work environment, where employees thrive and grow, is our ability to celebrate and value our differences in background, experiences and perspectives. In our recruitment process we welcome all professional people without consideration of age, colour, gender identity, national origin, physical or mental disability, ethnicity or religion.

Take technical ownership of our launched medical devices – driving product improvements, resolving technical challenges and ensuring long-term product performance.

Can you combine strong engineering judgement with hands-on technical work, take ownership of product design challenges and drive solutions through to completion?

Qufora develops intuitive medical devices that help people with chronic bowel disorders live a more fulfilled life. We are looking for an experienced Technical Product Owner to take technical responsibility for our launched products and help ensure their continued safety, performance and compliance.

Based at our headquarters in Allerød, north of Copenhagen, you will join our R&D organisation and work closely with colleagues across R&D, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs and Commercial, as well as external manufacturing partners.

Your role

As Technical Product Owner (TPO), you will have overall technical responsibility for the design of assigned launched products, including packaging and labelling. You will maintain a clear overview of their design status, performance, quality and technical documentation throughout their lifecycle.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you combine technical ownership with practical problem-solving. You will carry out technical work yourself where appropriate and involve specialists when their expertise is needed.

For smaller, straightforward changes, you will manage the activities yourself. For larger or more complex initiatives, a Project Manager will support planning and cross-functional coordination, while you retain responsibility for the technical scope and execution.

Your key responsibilities

• Maintain technical product ownership: Take over product knowledge and documentation from development and keep product requirements, specifications, risk assessments and design documentation up to date.

• Monitor product performance: Evaluate feedback from complaints, post-market surveillance and production data to identify technical issues, risks and opportunities for improvement.

• Investigate and resolve technical issues: Lead technical investigations and apply Structured Problem Solving, including root cause analysis, to address product failures and design-related quality issues.

• Drive product design changes: Assess technical impacts, initiate and manage Change Requests (CRs) and Change Orders (COs), and ensure that required design changes and documentation updates are completed.

• Plan and execute verification: Define acceptance criteria, plan verification activities, perform selected tests and analyse and document results, involving relevant specialists as needed.

• Ensure continued design compliance: Assess the technical impact of new standards, regulatory requirements and product changes, and ensure that necessary technical actions and documentation are completed.

• Drive product improvements: Identify and implement design improvements that strengthen product performance, quality, manufacturability, supply reliability or cost efficiency.

Your experience and qualifications

• A relevant degree in engineering or a related technical discipline, with minimum 5 years of experience in medical device development or medical device lifecycle management.

• Practical experience with design control, change control, risk management and technical documentation within an ISO 13485 quality management system.

• Working knowledge of ISO 14971, EU MDR and relevant medical device regulatory requirements.

• Experience with technical impact assessments, product requirements, risk assessments and verification of product design changes.

• Strong capabilities in Structured Problem Solving, technical investigations and interpretation of test and product performance data.

• A practical understanding of how product design, materials and manufacturing processes interact and affect product safety, performance and quality.

• Familiarity with PLM/PDM systems, controlled product documentation and engineering change processes.

• Professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

Experience with polymer components, injection moulding and external manufacturing partners is an advantage.

How you work

You are a structured, analytical and pragmatic engineer who combines sound technical judgement with a hands-on approach. You take ownership of challenges, work independently when appropriate and follow issues through to resolution.

You recognise when specialist expertise is needed and know how to bring the right people together to reach sound technical decisions.

You work closely with the Commercial Product Manager to align technical activities with customer and business needs, and collaborate with Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs and external manufacturing partners to understand dependencies and ensure that product design changes can be implemented effectively.

You communicate clearly, challenge assumptions constructively and balance product performance, patient safety, quality, supply and cost when evaluating technical solutions.

What we offer

A role with genuine technical responsibility for medical devices that make a difference in people's everyday lives.

You will join a relatively small and flat organisation with short decision paths and the opportunity to influence both product improvements and how we manage our products throughout their lifecycle.

At Qufora, you will work with a broad range of technical challenges, from design control and verification to product investigations and improvements. Your technical judgement and initiative will have a visible impact.

You will be part of an R&D organisation where we value technical expertise, practical problem-solving and collaboration – and where we believe that having fun along the way is just as important.

Interested?

If you enjoy taking technical ownership, solving engineering challenges and improving products already used by patients every day, we would like to hear from you. Please apply through LinkedIn with your CV and a brief description of your motivation for the role. We will review applications and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis.

Shape how AI transforms one of Denmark’s leading B2B businesses

AI is changing how we serve our customers, operate our business and create value. In TDC Erhverv, our goal is not simply to launch more AI use cases. We want to use AI to transform customer journeys, commercial activities, delivery and operations end to end.

We are therefore looking for a Head of AI, TDC Erhverv to set the direction and turn that goal into measurable business impact.

This is not primarily a technology role. It is a senior business transformation role with AI at its core.

You will shape and advance our B2B AI agenda. You will connect technology opportunities with strategic business priorities and bring together people and capabilities across the organization to turn AI potential into tangible customer and business value.

Your role

As Head of AI, you will be the senior orchestration point for the AI agenda across TDC Erhverv.

You will own and develop our AI strategy and roadmap and build a coherent portfolio of AI initiatives around customer journeys, business domains and end-to-end value chains.

You will identify where AI, process redesign, automation, data and technology can come together to create broader business transformation and where capabilities can be reused and scaled across the organization.

You will work closely with senior leaders across TDC Erhverv as well as Technology, data, architecture, security and other capabilities across TDC Brands. The role operates through a federated model, which means effective performance depends on your ability to create direction, mobilize highly skilled colleagues and lead through influence rather than formal authority.

Your responsibilities

You will:

• Set the strategic direction and ambition for AI across TDC Erhverv.

• Own and develop our B2B AI strategy, roadmap and portfolio.

• Identify and prioritize the AI opportunities with the greatest potential to create customer and business value.

• Connect individual AI opportunities into broader customer journey and end-to-end transformation agendas.

• Drive AI initiatives from opportunity and qualification through prioritization, delivery, adoption and scaling.

• Ensure clear business ownership, measurable outcomes and benefit realization.

• Reassess, reorder, or discontinue initiatives when business value, feasibility, or ownership is lacking.

• Build effective collaboration between business, Technology, data and other specialist capabilities.

• Strengthen AI adoption and capabilities across TDC Erhverv.

• Advise senior leadership on AI opportunities, priorities, investments, dependencies and risks.

• Represent TDC Erhverv in relevant internal and external AI forums and strategic partnerships.

Who are you?

We are looking for someone who combines AI understanding, solid business judgement and transformation leadership.

We don't expect you to build the models or write the code. But you need sufficient technological depth to understand what is possible, challenge the right questions and engage credibly with senior Technology, data and architecture stakeholders.

We expect that you:

• Have a solid grasp of generative AI, agentic AI, and the opportunities AI can create for large organizations.

• Have experience translating new technology into business strategy, transformation and measurable value.

• Can connect strategic goals with execution and prioritization.

• Demonstrate sound business judgment and evaluate opportunities using customer value, financial impact, feasibility, scalability, and risk.

• Are comfortable navigating complex organizations and leading cross-functional agendas without necessarily having formal authority.

• Can engage senior stakeholders in a constructive way and help shape decisions.

• Communicate clearly and effectively, making complex topics easy for diverse audiences to understand and connect with.

• Bring curiosity and an external perspective on how AI is changing businesses, industries and customer expectations.

• Understand the importance of responsible AI, governance, security and data protection.

What success looks like

We will not measure success by how many AI pilots we launch.

Success means that AI creates documented improvements in our business, including better customer experience, increased productivity and efficiency, better commercial performance and scalable ways of working. It also means building an organization where AI becomes embedded in relevant workflows, rather than remaining a collection of stand-alone experiments.

jobs.description:
Are you an experimental physicist eager to push light–matter interaction to its extremes? 

We offer a PhD scholarship at DTU Electro, where you will trap light in nanoscale optical cavities coupled to highly nonlinear 2D materials, and control them to let light interact with light far more strongly than conventional devices allow.

To trap and release light on demand, we use photonic crystal cavities in thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), whose strong electro-optic effect allows fast electrical control. Our team has recently demonstrated ultracompact TFLN cavities used as modulators [1], with electrically controllable coupling to waveguides [2], and as multiport switches [3]. The project builds on these results and shares fabrication efforts with our collaborators at Harvard University, who pioneered the TFLN platform [4].

Photons interact only through a material nonlinearity, and in conventional static cavities the interaction time is fundamentally bounded, which dynamically coupled cavities can overcome [5]. You will combine such cavities with atomically thin 2D semiconductors with exceptionally strong nonlinearities to explore a largely uncharted dynamic regime of nonlinear optics, aiming to generate quantum states of light, such as squeezed light, at ultralow energies. The project is part of the Center for Nanophotonics (NanoPhoton), a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will drive the experimental work in the project from device design to demonstration, working closely with PhD students, postdocs, and senior researchers at DTU and our collaborators at Harvard University. Depending on your interests, you will have the opportunity to:

• Design photonic crystal cavities and circuits using electromagnetic and multiphysics simulations.
• Fabricate devices in DTU Nanolab’s state-of-the-art cleanroom.
• Integrate 2D materials with photonic chips.
• Characterize devices using high-speed electro-optic, pulsed-laser, and quantum-optical measurements.
• Compare your experiments with theoretical models of cavity dynamics.
• Present your results at international conferences and in leading journals.
You are curious and driven, enjoy hands-on laboratory work, and take ownership of the progress and quality of your work.

Required qualifications:

• A strong background in optics or photonics.
• Experimental experience in optics or photonics, e.g., from your master’s project.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

• Nanofabrication or integrated photonics.
• Nonlinear or quantum optics, or 2D materials.
